description: 10 construction-industry concept terms, each with 5 human-authored (context, goal) pairs. Used as the seed for Barrett-aligned self-generation and LoRA fine-tuning.

instances.context: The facade restoration crew must erect scaffolding around a 12-storey residential block before brick repointing can begin.
instances.goal: provide safe elevated access for workers at every floor level

instances.context: A scaffold tube struck a passing pedestrian after an unsecured clamp failed during a storm on a city-centre site.
instances.goal: identify the root cause of the structural failure to prevent recurrence

instances.context: The project manager is planning scaffold hire duration against the programme to minimise cost while keeping access live for bricklayers.
instances.goal: optimise scaffold hire period against the construction programme

instances.context: The site supervisor must inspect the scaffold each Monday morning before operatives are permitted to use it for the working week.
instances.goal: verify structural integrity and compliance before permitting access

instances.context: The scaffold contractor has submitted a design drawing for a complex birdcage scaffold over a listed building roof requiring temporary propping.
instances.goal: review the scaffold design for structural adequacy and heritage compliance

instances.context: The contractor proposes to remove an internal wall to open up the ground floor plan of a Victorian terrace, and the structural engineer must assess whether it is load-bearing.
instances.goal: determine whether removal requires a structural steel beam and temporary propping

instances.context: During a demolition survey a site operative breached a load-bearing masonry wall without authorisation, causing partial floor collapse above.
instances.goal: assess structural risk and establish an emergency propping strategy

instances.context: The architect's drawing labels a partition as non-structural, but the contractor suspects it is load-bearing based on its position and the joist direction above.
instances.goal: resolve the structural ambiguity before proceeding with the works

instances.context: A homeowner wants to convert the loft, and the structural engineer must calculate whether the existing ceiling joists can carry the new floor loading or must be replaced.
instances.goal: determine whether the existing structure can carry the proposed additional load

instances.context: The fire compartmentation strategy requires a load-bearing concrete core to maintain structural stability for at least 90 minutes under fire conditions.
instances.goal: confirm the structural element meets the required fire resistance period

terms.grammatical_frame: plural noun, head of noun phrase, attributive modifier=construction

instances.context: The precast concrete panel contractor has delivered units 18 mm out of plumb, and the architect must decide whether this falls within acceptable tolerances for the curtain wall system.
instances.goal: determine whether the deviation is acceptable or requires remedial action

instances.context: The steelwork erector and the brickwork subcontractor are disputing whose responsibility it is to accommodate a 22 mm horizontal setting-out discrepancy between the steel frame and the masonry skin.
instances.goal: assign contractual responsibility for remedying the setting-out discrepancy

instances.context: The floor screed has been laid with surface regularity deviations of ±6 mm under a 3 m straightedge, exceeding the TR34 specification for a racking warehouse floor.
instances.goal: assess whether the floor performance will be acceptable for the racking system

instances.context: The mechanical engineer is designing a pipe run through precast planks and needs to specify the hole-position tolerance so that the structural engineer can confirm no rebar is cut.
instances.goal: set a buildable hole-position tolerance that protects structural integrity

instances.context: A cladding contractor is pricing a tender and must allow for the dimensional tolerances in the primary steel frame when sizing the fixing brackets.
instances.goal: price the bracket adjustment range to absorb expected frame tolerances

instances.context: A new groundworks subcontractor is mobilising 12 operatives to site on Monday and the site manager must complete the site induction before any work begins.
instances.goal: ensure all operatives understand site-specific hazards and emergency procedures before starting work

instances.context: An HSE inspector arrived unannounced and found a labourer on site without a record of having completed the site induction.
instances.goal: demonstrate compliance with CDM regulations and correct the gap in the induction record

instances.context: The project involves working adjacent to a live railway and the site induction must cover Network Rail safe-system-of-work requirements in addition to the standard site rules.
instances.goal: incorporate railway-specific safety requirements into the induction briefing

instances.context: A site induction was delivered verbally with no written record kept, and following a near-miss the contractor cannot prove the injured operative received safety training.
instances.goal: establish an auditable induction record to support the incident investigation

instances.context: The main contractor has 15 different subcontractors on site simultaneously and needs a scalable induction process that can handle 20 new starters on any given morning.
instances.goal: design an efficient induction system that maintains quality while handling high throughput

terms.grammatical_frame: gerund noun phrase, head=curing, prepositional complement=of concrete

instances.context: The concrete slab for a warehouse floor has been poured in August and the site engineer must specify the curing regime to prevent plastic shrinkage cracking in the hot, dry weather.
instances.goal: prevent early-age cracking by maintaining adequate moisture and temperature at the slab surface

instances.context: A bridge deck pour will take place in January and the structural engineer must specify the minimum curing period before traffic loading can be applied.
instances.goal: determine the minimum curing period required to achieve the specified design strength

instances.context: The post-tensioned transfer slab cannot be stressed until the concrete has achieved a minimum cube strength, and the curing regime determines when stressing can begin.
instances.goal: predict when the concrete will reach the minimum stressing strength based on the curing conditions

instances.context: The specification requires 7 days wet curing using polythene sheeting, but the contractor has stripped the formwork after 24 hours citing programme pressure.
instances.goal: assess whether early formwork removal and inadequate curing has compromised the structural integrity

instances.context: The client is requesting a fast-track programme and asks whether accelerated curing using steam or heating can reduce the curing period on the precast element production line.
instances.goal: evaluate whether accelerated curing methods can safely reduce the production cycle time

instances.context: The carpenter is planning when to strike the wall formwork on a retaining wall pour so that the concrete surface is not damaged and the required strength has been achieved.
instances.goal: determine the earliest safe time to remove the formwork without damaging the concrete

instances.context: The formwork for a transfer beam has deflected 18 mm at mid-span under the wet concrete load, and the structural engineer must assess whether this exceeds the allowable camber.
instances.goal: assess whether formwork deflection will produce a beam with unacceptable sag after striking

instances.context: The contractor is comparing proprietary system formwork against traditional timber shuttering for a repetitive core-wall lift cycle and must evaluate cost and cycle-time implications.
instances.goal: select the most cost-effective and programme-efficient formwork system for the core wall

instances.context: A formwork collapse on a multi-storey in-situ concrete frame has resulted in three operatives being injured, and the HSE has issued a prohibition notice.
instances.goal: identify the immediate cause of the formwork collapse and prevent further incidents

instances.context: The architect requires an off-form concrete finish to Grade F3 standard and the formwork contractor must specify the panel type, release agent, and pour sequence.
instances.goal: specify the formwork system and pour methodology to achieve the specified off-form concrete finish

instances.context: The main contractor is procuring a mechanical and electrical sub-contractor for a hospital fit-out and must carry out pre-qualification checks before placing the order.
instances.goal: verify the sub-contractor's financial stability, technical competence, and insurance before appointment

instances.context: A domestic sub-contractor has left site mid-contract without completing the structural steelwork, leaving the programme 3 weeks behind and the frame exposed to weather.
instances.goal: recover the programme and protect the partially erected steel frame from further damage

instances.context: The main contractor intends to novate the design sub-contractor's appointment from the employer to themselves at the point of contract award.
instances.goal: transfer design liability from the employer to the main contractor through novation

instances.context: The main contractor has subcontracted 90% of the works by value and the project manager must decide how to manage design coordination between five sub-contractors working simultaneously.
instances.goal: establish a design coordination protocol that prevents interface clashes between concurrent sub-contractor packages

instances.context: A sub-contractor has submitted a loss and expense claim following a 6-week employer delay and the quantity surveyor must assess the entitlement under the sub-contract conditions.
instances.goal: evaluate the sub-contractor's contractual entitlement to loss and expense for the employer-caused delay

instances.context: A roofer is working on a fragile roof without a hard hat, high-visibility vest, or fall-arrest harness, and the site manager has just noticed from below.
instances.goal: immediately stop the unsafe work and enforce compliance with the required PPE

instances.context: The occupational health advisor is reviewing hand-arm vibration exposure for concrete breaker operators and must specify whether anti-vibration gloves are required as PPE.
instances.goal: determine whether anti-vibration gloves provide sufficient protection for the exposure duration

instances.context: A worker suffered a serious eye injury from cement splash, and the investigation found that safety glasses were available on site but not being worn during the mixing operation.
instances.goal: identify why PPE compliance failed and implement controls to prevent recurrence

instances.context: The project involves confined space entry into a sewer and the site manager must specify the breathing apparatus and PPE requirements for the entry team and standby rescue team.
instances.goal: specify the correct respiratory PPE and rescue equipment for a confined-space entry in a sewer environment

instances.context: The main contractor is reviewing PPE costs and the procurement manager proposes switching to a cheaper hard hat supplier; the safety manager must assess whether the cheaper product meets EN397.
instances.goal: verify the alternative hard hat meets the required safety standard before approving the switch

instances.context: The contract administrator is inspecting the completed building to decide whether to issue the practical completion certificate despite a list of 47 snagging items still outstanding.
instances.goal: determine whether the outstanding defects prevent practical completion being certified

instances.context: The employer wants to take possession of a completed wing of a phased hospital project before the rest of the building is finished, and the contractor disputes whether sectional completion provisions apply.
instances.goal: establish whether the contract permits sectional practical completion for the occupied wing

instances.context: Practical completion was certified 3 months late due to the contractor's programme overrun, and the employer is seeking to deduct liquidated damages at the rate stated in the contract.
instances.goal: calculate the liquidated damages entitlement based on the certified delay to practical completion

instances.context: The contractor is claiming that practical completion was achieved on the programmed date even though the certificate was not issued, arguing the employer had beneficial use of the building.
instances.goal: assess whether beneficial occupation by the employer constitutes de facto practical completion

instances.context: The defects liability period begins at practical completion, and the contractor needs to understand when their obligation to return and remedy defects formally expires.
instances.goal: determine the start and end dates of the defects liability period relative to the practical completion certificate

instances.context: A structural engineer's design error caused a retaining wall to fail 18 months after completion, and the question is whether the engineer's professional indemnity insurance covers the claim.
instances.goal: establish whether the design error falls within the engineer's covered professional liability

instances.context: The main contractor is arguing that a nominated sub-contractor's defective waterproofing is the employer's liability because the employer selected the sub-contractor.
instances.goal: determine which party bears contractual liability for the nominated sub-contractor's defective work

instances.context: The building contract includes a net contribution clause limiting each consultant's liability to their proportionate share of the loss, and the employer's solicitor is challenging its enforceability.
instances.goal: assess whether the net contribution clause is enforceable to limit the consultant's liability exposure

instances.context: A visitor slipped on an unguarded excavation edge on a construction site at night and is pursuing a personal injury claim against the main contractor.
instances.goal: assess the main contractor's occupier's liability exposure and the adequacy of their site security measures

instances.context: The contractor is reviewing whether to accept a design-and-build contract with unlimited liability for fitness for purpose of the completed building.
instances.goal: quantify the risk exposure of accepting unlimited fitness-for-purpose liability before signing the contract
